historical_defects.claim_says: A held later order, Executive Order 6513 of December 18, 1933, approves "an Amendment (Number I)" to this code
historical_defects.source_says: The amendment is Executive Order 6513-I (APP heading 'Executive Order 6513-I—Code of Fair Competition for the Cast Iron Soil Pipe Industry (Amendment Number I)'; WPA list '6513-1: Dec. 18 Amendment to the Code...'). Executive Order 6513 (no suffix) of the same date is a different order, 'Amendment of Executive Order No. 6433-A' (Special Industrial Recovery Board / National Emergency Council; WPA p. 557).

historical_defects.claim_says: A held later order, Executive Order 6885 of October 25, 1934, approves an amended code for the Builders Supplies Trade
historical_defects.source_says: The amending order is Executive Order 6885-A of October 25, 1934 (APP heading 'Executive Order 6885-A—Amended Code of Fair Competition for the Builders Supplies Trade'; WPA p. 594 '6885-A'). Executive Order 6885 is a different order of October 23, 1934 amending rules for the Army and Navy General Hospital, Hot Springs, Arkansas.

historical_defects.claim_says: Executive Order 6925 of December 19, 1934, which places the construction operations of the Cinders, Ashes, and Scavenger Trade under it
historical_defects.source_says: The order is Executive Order 6925-A of December 19, 1934 (APP heading 'Executive Order 6925-A—Canceling Order Approving Code for the Cinders, Ashes and Scavenger Trade'; WPA p. 598). Its operative command cancels the order approving the Cinders, Ashes and Scavenger Trade code; only its recital states that upon cancellation the construction operations 'will be subject to' the Construction Industry code. Executive Order 6925 is a different order of December 18, 1934 (Tongass National Forest land restoration).

historical_defects.claim_says: registered Federal Register original (10 FR, issue of 1945-04-27 ...)
historical_defects.source_says: The cited original is the issue of Tuesday, April 17, 1945 (URL FR-1945-04-17; 10 FR 4057; filed Apr. 14, 1945). The 'April 27' reading comes from the garbled OCR masthead ('.Apri/ 27, 2025'); April 27, 1945 was a Friday. The rationale contradicts the claim's own original_representation.
